title: Vedic Hymns, Part I: Hymns to the Maruts, Rudra, Vayu and Vata
altTitles: Sacred Books of the East, vol. 32
dateDisplay: Hymns composed c. 1500–1000 BCE; translation published 1891
attributionNote: The hymns are anonymous. The selection, translation, introduction and notes are F. Max Müller's, the first volume of his planned translation of the whole Rigveda for the Sacred Books of the East.
description: The first volume of Müller's Vedic Hymns translates the Rigvedic hymns to the storm-gods and the winds: the Maruts, Rudra, Vayu and Vata, with the hymn to the unknown god that opens the selection. Müller's introductions and notes discuss the gods, the metres and the difficulties of the text, and the volume is as much a work of Vedic scholarship as a translation.
historicalContext: Friedrich Max Müller (1823–1900) edited the Rigveda with Sayana's commentary and was the general editor of the Sacred Books of the East. This volume appeared in 1891 as SBE 32; his death left the projected complete translation unfinished, and SBE 46 continued the series with Oldenberg's hymns to Agni.
availabilityNote: Complete as published: the introduction, the hymns to the Maruts, Rudra, Vayu and Vata with translation and notes, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one hymn per chapter. The volume's appendices, indexes and corrigenda are not part of the work.
